title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We want safer, production-ready defaults and automation that reduce per-token costs without regressions to latency or quality. This PR centralizes autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, adds first-class quantization profile support for common model families, and ships a unit-economics (UEcon) CLI + dashboard integration used by the cost optimization team to recommend settings. Summary of changes: 1) Runtime defaults and autotune: introduced a new AutotuneDefaults module that selects initial batching window, max batch size, and cache TTL based on observed seq length distributions and customer SLOs. Defaults are conservative for latency-sensitive routes and aggressive for background/embeddings traffic. 2) KV cache defaults: added prefix caching heuristics and TTLs keyed by route/model combo; integrated with the runtime cache manager and added metrics to expose cache hit/miss by prefix length. 3) Quantization profiles: new on-disk profiles that map model family + hardware to recommended quantization knobs (int8, int4 variants, per-channel vs per-tensor). Profiles include expected throughput/cost multipliers we use in the UEcon calculator. 4) Unit-economics tooling: a uecon CLI that ingests historical request traces and current infra costs and outputs recommended config bundles (batching + cache + quant profile) with an estimated cost delta and quality sensitivity notes. Includes a dashboard widget and a small API endpoint for programmatic pulls. 5) E2E safety and rollout: canary rollout config for 10% of traffic, automatic rollback on latency or quality regression thresholds, and a manual opt-out toggle per-customer. Tests and validation: added integration tests for batching heuristics, simulation-based regressions for quantization profiles, and end-to-end tests for the uecon CLI using synthetic traces. Backwards compatibility: all changes are opt-in by default; projects can opt into autotune via route flags. Migration: added a migration that seeds default quant profiles for onboarded models. Checklist: - [x] AutotuneDefaults module implemented - [x] KV prefix caching heuristics added - [x] Quantization profile schema and two families added (openlm/ggml-like and transformer-x) - [x] UEcon CLI + dashboard integration - [x] Canary + rollback logic and tests - [x] Docs and release notes updated Rollout plan: staged canary across infra zones for 2 weeks, watchers on p50/p90/p99 latency, token cost, cache hit rate, model output quality samples. Related: ENG-1234, PM-4321.

release_notes: Introduce AutotuneDefaults for safer batching and cache defaults; quantization profile support for model-family-specific recommendations; UEcon CLI and dashboard integration that suggests cost-saving bundles. Opt-in by default with canary rollout and rollback safeguards.

Run UEcon recommendations on top 50 customer traces and validate output quality
Schedule ops runbook update to include autotune rollback steps
notes: This PR centralizes several cost-optimization efforts and is intentionally conservative about defaults. Customers must opt-in to aggressive autotune. The UEcon tooling is designed to be auditable (JSON output) and can be used by SRE/Platform teams to recommend safe rollouts.
